correctness.rationale: In T_n all nonadjacent pairs are at distance two, so the forbidden triples are induced three-vertex paths. Components of a selected induced cluster graph are pairwise intersecting edge families on mutually disjoint supports in K_n; one incident pair ab,ac shows the only non-star possibility is the whole triangle abc. Unused vertices contribute singleton blocks. The weights at support sizes 1, 2, 3 and k>=4 are 1, z, 3z^2+z^3 and kz^{k-1}, yielding the first EGF. Maximality excludes two unused vertices, two-edge stars, and any unused vertex when a selected star exists. Conversely, an edge crossing occupied components meets a selected edge in each, and those two old edges are disjoint; this supplies the general crossing case in line 48. An added leaf edge in a star of at least three edges or an edge from an unused vertex into a triangle also creates a forbidden triple. Thus the maximal modes are full coverage by allowed components, or a single unused vertex with only triangles, giving exactly the second EGF including the formal n=0,1 terms. For maximum size, each nontriangle support loses exactly one selected edge relative to its vertex count, giving the claimed residue cases. In the full-coverage maximal mode, twice the edge count minus n is additive: zero for a K2, 3 for a triangle, and k-2 for a k-vertex star (k>=4). This corrects the informal half-support arithmetic in line 58: a triangle and a five-vertex star each have excess 3/2 above half their support. For odd n, an odd component is necessary, the least doubled excess is 3, and equality is exactly one triangle or one five-vertex star plus disjoint pairs. The unused-vertex mode never ties the minima for n>=2. Counting labels gives both extremal formulas. Private replay /workspace/branches/replay/triangle.py and triangle.txt used actual shortest paths and all legal subset extensions, reproducing both complete arrays through n=7 and checking extremal coefficients by exact extraction through n=15. The proof, not these finite checks, covers all n.
